grades.what_is_wrong: Rider says it turns wide and drops out of ruts, but the answer talks him out of the standard first fix (more fork tube showing / more front bias) and gives a stock-clicker table and a question instead of a change. Stock 5.0/54 springs match tester data; the stock clicker values I could not verify (unsure). At 205 lb plus gear he is past what the stock springs suit, and the answer never says that.
grades.better_answer_would: Tell him to set sag at about 105 mm, slide the forks up 2-3 mm or slow fork rebound 2 clicks so the front stays in the rut, and say that at about 225 lb geared he should plan on a 5.2 fork and 56 shock spring.

grades.what_is_wrong: His complaint is that it runs wide and won't hold a rut, yet the answer moves the tubes from 6 to 4 mm showing. That raises the front and slows turn-in, so it works against what he wants and contradicts the goal he already gave. It also asks whether he wants it to turn tighter (he already said so), cites an odd 'top-plug' stock reference, and ends with a 'save with the button' line.
grades.better_answer_would: Say that 6 mm is already on the high side (testers run about 3 mm), so the turning fix is sag or fork rebound rather than more height, and give one change to test.

grades.what_is_wrong: The click directions are right, but it never commits. On braking bumps that kick back hard, softer compression is usually the right direction, while slowing rebound usually makes the fork pack. A tuner would say keep the compression change and put rebound back to 12.
grades.better_answer_would: Say the compression change was probably good and the rebound change probably bad for braking bumps: go back to 12 out on rebound and test.

grades.what_is_wrong: It reads 'more rebound than I'd like' as a rear that springs back, which is a reasonable guess, and gets the click direction right. Sag of 90-100 mm and a 54 N/mm stock spring look consistent with 2025 data; I could not verify the 12-out stock rebound (unsure). It doesn't mention that a C rider at 175 lb is fine on stock springs except for that one sentence.
grades.better_answer_would: The same answer, trimmed, leading with 'set sag to about 95 mm, then go in 2 clicks on rebound'.

grades.what_is_wrong: The order of work is sound, but it can't give the stock fork height, so the question about when to set fork height is only half answered. It ends with an app 'Start a guided job' prompt. I could not verify the 13/12 stock fork clickers (unsure).
grades.better_answer_would: Give Yamaha's stock fork height for this bike and say: reset clickers, set sag, then use fork height only for a steering problem.

grades.what_is_wrong: A solid split between first-hit harshness and harshness that builds, with good mechanical checks (chain, linkage, tire) and KTM's baseline. It still gives no first change to make.
grades.better_answer_would: Add a first test: if it skips, open low-speed compression 2 clicks; if it packs, speed rebound 2 clicks.

grades.what_is_wrong: Reducing sag to 100 mm and leaving HSC alone is reasonable, and it correctly notes that raising the rear sharpens steering. It treats him as stock-sprung even though he is resprung (5.2 shock spring at 140 lb is stiff), so 'free sag shows a soft spring' is unlikely; bottoming with a stiff spring points more to damping or shock condition. I could not verify Yamaha's 1/6-turn HSC step (unsure).
grades.better_answer_would: Note that a 5.2 spring at 140 lb should not bottom in G-outs, so have the shock checked or add HSC, and expect less sag to make the twitchy front worse.

grades.what_is_wrong: Correct and clear, and the table puts the two adjustments side by side. It runs slightly long.
grades.better_answer_would: As written, maybe two lines shorter.

grades.what_is_wrong: The offset/trail direction is correct and it correctly says neither clamp fixes harshness. The fork data fits KTM's (10.6-10.7 bar, 12/18). It could have given a concrete air-fork step (for example, drop 0.1-0.2 bar or open compression 2 clicks).
grades.better_answer_would: Same answer, plus one concrete air or compression test for sharp edges.

grades.what_is_wrong: Checking steering for binding is a fair point, but the rider asked how to get more flex and less handlebar shock. It skips the usual levers: bar bend and material, rubber-mounted or flex clamps, tire pressure, and engine-mount torque. It also misses that 8-10 out on the clickers and 105 mm sag after a respring deserve review.
grades.better_answer_would: Check the steering head, then try softer bars or bar mounts, 12-13 psi tires, and opening fork compression 2 clicks, one change at a time.

grades.what_is_wrong: Useful KTM and tuner baselines, and it rightly says not to run extra sag just because he is tall. It never names the shock spring a 250 lb rider needs (well past the stock rate, roughly 48-50 N/mm), and the table is long.
grades.better_answer_would: Give the spring range for 250 lb geared, then 105/35 sag and the starting clickers.

grades.what_is_wrong: Correct logic, and judging over the whole lap is good advice. It asks 'fork or tire pressure' even though the KTM air-fork thread makes it obvious.
